headline: Waaree Renewable - :  Expects Interest And Depreciation To Steady, Aiming To Cut Acquisition Debt Soon - Concall Update

Waaree Renewable - :  Solar EPC Will Drive Core Growth With T&D Business, Over INR 20,000 Crore Order Pipeline. Company Anticipates Strong Opportunities in Renewable Energy, BESS, and T&D Due to Policy Support and Increasing Demand.

Waaree Renewable - :  Expects To Keep Consolidated EBITDA Margins Over 15% And Foresees T&D Segment Margins, Currently At 9-10%, To Rise In The Coming Quarters; The Unexecuted Order Book Exceeding INR 5,500 Crores, With INR 3,300 Crores From Solar EPC And BESS, Is Expected To Generate Revenue In The Next Three To Four Quarters.

Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services - :  CLSA on Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services Maintains Outperform, Target Price ₹405; Q2FY27 PPOP/PAT beat estimates by 5%/12%, with PPOP growing 20% YoY on higher fees and lower credit costs. Asset quality improved, with Stage 2+3 loans at a multi-year low, while accelerating disbursements should support future AUM growth; fixed-rate lending and floating-rate borrowings could pressure spreads if rates rise.

NALCO - :  Nomura on NALCO Initiates Neutral, Target Price ₹320; cites limited growth initiatives and an unfavourable earnings mix. Nomura expects aluminium-sector value creation to increasingly depend on resource control and operational efficiency rather than commodity-price exposure.

Eternal - :  CLSA on Eternal Maintains High Conviction Outperform, Target Price ₹506; Q2 growth was broadly in line, but Blinkit’s adjusted EBITDA missed elevated expectations amid faster store additions, while food delivery margins are expected to remain flat near term as the company reinvests. CLSA raises FY27–29 PAT estimates by 38–78% to reflect faster expansion and higher marketing costs, but shifts expected steady-state profitability from FY28 to FY29.

Eternal - :  JPMorgan on Eternal Maintains Overweight, Target Price ₹420; food-delivery net order value (NOV) growth accelerated for the fifth consecutive quarter to 21% YoY, while Blinkit NOV rose 22% QoQ and adjusted EBITDA margin improved 30bps to 0.9%. Management raised Blinkit store targets to 3,500 by March 2027 and 5,000 by March 2028, reiterating a 60% quick-commerce NOV CAGR target through FY29.

Indian Hotels - :  Nomura on Indian Hotels Company Maintains Buy, Target Price ₹850; Q2FY27 revenue/EBITDA grew 22%/24% YoY, beating consensus by 5%/3%. FY27 revenue growth guidance was raised to 15–17% from 12–14%, with hotel revenue expected to grow 17–19%; Nomura expects mid-to-high-teens consolidated EBITDA growth in H2FY27 and FY28.

Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services - :  HSBC on Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services Maintains Buy, cuts Target Price to ₹340, implying 1.5x FY28E book value per share versus 1.7x previously; higher fee income and lower credit costs drove a Q2 earnings beat, while estimates factor in stronger AUM growth alongside pressure on NIMs and fees.

Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services - :  Nomura on Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services Maintains Buy, cuts Target Price to ₹400; Q2FY27 net profit was 14% above estimates and asset quality remained healthy, but FY27–29 net profit estimates are cut by 1–9%; insurance distribution reforms remain a risk.

Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services - :  Citi on Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services Maintains Buy, Target Price ₹420; PAT rose 55% YoY, beating estimates despite 30bps NIM compression, as credit costs remained contained and fee income supported RoA at 2.2%. Disbursements grew 22% YoY and AUM growth exceeded 15%, while improved collections and asset quality supported management’s guidance despite rural headwinds.
Hindalco - :  Nomura on Hindalco Industries Initiates Buy, Target Price ₹1,100; believes the market has yet to fully recognise the value of the company’s expansion projects.
Vedanta Aluminium: Nomura on Vedanta Aluminium Initiates Buy, Target Price ₹500; sees a favourable reset in the company’s cost structure, supporting its investment case.
